Destination guide

Tanzania delivers some of Africa’s most cinematic safari landscapes, from Serengeti migration scenes to the Ngorongoro Crater and Zanzibar’s coast. The northern circuit links Tarangire, Ngorongoro, and distinct Serengeti zones, while the south offers lower-density parks and Zanzibar adds a living Swahili heritage landscape rather than beach time alone.

Photos: Giles Laurent (CC BY-SA 4.0) · Eric Kilby (CC BY-SA 2.0). Displayed images may be resized or cropped. Photo details.

Getting around

Most trips flow through Arusha, Kilimanjaro International Airport, or Dar es Salaam depending on whether the route is inland safari or coast-first.

Best time

June to October is the cleanest safari season for much of the north, while January to March works well for southern Serengeti calving and beach add-ons.

Planning notes

Most first-time routes flow through Arusha, Tarangure or Lake Manyara, Ngorongoro, Serengeti, and Zanzibar. Migration goals should decide the Serengeti zone, while beach nights work best after the safari rather than between park transfers.
